newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan March long-term prime seen unchanged-traders.
newsitem.headline: Japan March long-term prime seen unchanged-traders.

text.p: Japan's long-term prime rate is likely to be left unchanged at a record-low 2.5 percent in March, bond traders said on Thursday.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) is scheduled to announce its long-term prime rate next Monday afternoon.
The prime rate, at which long-term credit banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, was cut by 0.2 percentage point to a record-low 2.5 percent in December.
The IBJ customarily sets its long-term prime rate 0.9 percentage point above its five-year debenture coupon rate.
The IBJ's February five-year bank debentures, with a coupon rate of 1.6 percent, were traded at a yield of 1.63 percent on Thursday, bond traders said.
Judging from current market conditions, the long-term prime rate is likely to be left unchanged in March, the traders said.
